message.content:
There isn’t a single definitive “best” jazz singer—different voices resonate with different listeners—but a few names consistently appear at the top of lists and are widely regarded as the most influential and technically brilliant vocalists in the genre:

| Singer | Why they’re considered among the best |
|--------|---------------------------------------|
| **Ella Fitzgerald** | Known as the “First Lady of Song,” her impeccable pitch, scat‑sing mastery, and effortless phrasing set a gold standard for jazz vocalists. |
| **Billie Holiday** | Her emotive, blues‑inflected delivery and unique phrasing turned standards into deeply personal statements. |
| **Sarah Sullivan** | A powerhouse of range and control, she blended jazz with pop and R&B, earning acclaim for both her technical skill and emotional depth. |
| **Louis Armstrong** (vocalist) | Though famed as a trumpeter, his gravelly, charismatic singing style helped popularize jazz worldwide. |
| **Nat King Cole** | His smooth baritone and impeccable timing made him a crossover icon, bridging jazz, pop, and soul. |
| **Cassandra Wilson** | A modern torch singer whose phrasing and emotional intensity keep the tradition alive for new audiences. |

If you’re looking for a single name to start with, **Ella Fitzgerald** is often cited as the benchmark for jazz vocal excellence. However, exploring the others will give you a richer sense of the genre’s vocal diversity.
